hook: SCP-1500 opens as a quiet, almost tender case: a man slowly turning into a plant who asks only to be left alone while it finishes. Keep reading past the point where it seems to end. The page holds two documents, and the order they come in is the whole trick.
whyItMatters: This is an article whose structure does most of the storytelling. Nothing in the first part reads as false, and the payoff comes from setting two sets of containment rules next to each other and letting you compare them. It is a compact lesson in how much a Foundation file can hide inside perfectly ordinary procedure.
thingsToNotice:
The first document is the cover story the second one orders into existence: a fake file meant to discourage investigation or rescue attempts. Its rules (no one enters, no cameras, no windows) are framed as protecting a fragile, photosynthesizing Zachary Callahan; in the real document the same rules exist to protect staff from what is actually in the cell.

The real SCP-1500 is a featureless grey-green humanoid with a swollen abdomen and long multi-jointed limbs. Anyone who sees it suffers headaches, nausea and mounting fear for a few minutes, blacks out for about fifteen seconds, and wakes up seeing a white man named Zachary Callahan whom they remember as an old friend.

The addenda escalate quietly. A senator recalls a childhood fishing trip with a Zach Callahan who never lived nearby, newer victims remember it as a parent, a lost love or a relative they feel protective and adoring toward, and by the last entry around 23,000 people are affected, disproportionately political figures, military figures and Foundation staff. The file ends with a request to upgrade it to Keter.
